title: Wallace & Grmit: The Curse of the Were-Rabbit
review: I forgot Wallace went on ozempic. The villain is like a Tory version of Nigel Thornberry, who himself is obviously a Lib Dem. It ends in a similar way to {Midsommar} for him. Having studied the plot, I think they have very carefully managed to make it watertight. Wallace actually turns into the were rabbit physically, even though it was only a brainwashing experiment, because of the extra moon power he uses. They show you a calendar so that you know there are only a few days of consecutive full moons. This is part of the lineage from {One Hundred and One Dalmatians} to {Minions}. The shorter episodes are sharper because they had to be be incredibly efficient with time, but they've correctly identified that the characters can remain beloved throughout a feature length film, only if it happens every 20 years. We aren't oversaturated with content like other family characters, and {Shaun the Sheep} occupies a different space and demographic. It feels tedious to even bother mentioning this, but the CGI has aged poorly, while the claymation looks just as perfect as the day it was released.
